summary: Inventory application is serving on node1 TCP port 8181 under an enforcing AppArmor profile and persists across restart. Ubuntu 16.04.7 and kernel 4.4.0-210 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Created a Python 3.5 standard-library inventory service and persistent inventory data.
Added and loaded a least-privilege `inventory-app` AppArmor profile in enforce mode.
Verified health and inventory endpoints through node1's managed IP.
Restarted node1 exactly once and verified its changed boot identity and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Serve the inventory application over TCP port 8181
evidence.summary: Direct requests through node1's managed address returned healthy status and inventory data; `ss` showed Python listening on `*:8181` before and after restart.

All 14 AppArmor profiles were enforcing, zero were in complain mode, and the live inventory process reported `inventory-app (enforce)` before and after restart. No post-start or post-boot denials were present.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel and use legacy-compatible software
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 16.04.7 LTS, kernel 4.4.0-210-generic, and installed Python 3.5.2 were verified before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart and recovery sequence
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID 225ffbf7-477b-4e25-bbae-e26343dd98bd was captured; restart was acknowledged; node returned with boot ID f69ba75d-5ff2-497c-8d6a-c8cc5e985f39; enabled service, listener, endpoints, persisted data, and enforcing MAC confinement all recovered.
